Sure, hooktube doesn't actually host anything like youtube does. Youtube/Google has all the servers and spends big money on data centers, whereas hooktube only has a small server hosted by cloudflare and directs that smaller server to "point" at youtube's servers. Specifically, the "watch?v=" is really just the way youtube sets up their server to organize data in some logical manner.

The link:

youtu.be/FEbtrlYQuzk

will redirect you to 

"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FEbtrlYQuzk&feature=youtu.be"

The link:

"https://www.youtube.com/FEbtrlYQuzk"

should return a 404 error, because that doesn't fit youtube's syntax requirements.

However, when you sub in "hook" for "you" in either of those links, hooktube points to:

"https://youtube.com/watch?v=FEbtrlYQuzk"

which doesn't have the feature portion appended to it, because you weren't redirected from a shortened link.

So why do we do this? The advantage of using a hooktube link over a youtube link is that information is passed along in a different kind of way between servers and other servers versus servers and end users. Servers don't count towards ad revenue like end users do, because servers are just machines. Hooktube takes advantage of this rule of internet communication by cutting out the ads for us which saves bandwidth and time and prevents google from making money off hooktube links.
